title: useMutation
description: Learn how to modify server data with useMutation, handle all mutation states, and reset for reusable forms.

data.text: While `useQuery` is for fetching data, **useMutation** is for changing it. Mutations create, update, or delete records on your server. Unlike queries â€” which run automatically â€” mutations only fire when you explicitly call `mutate()`. React Query gives you detailed state tracking so you can show loading spinners, success messages, and error feedback to the user.

terms.definition: A React Query hook for performing data-changing operations (create, update, delete) on a server.
The async function passed to useMutation that performs the actual server request.
A boolean that is true while the mutation function is executing (React Query v5 equivalent of isLoading).
The function returned by useMutation that triggers the mutation when called.

data.text: React Query tracks five key states on every mutation object. Understanding each one lets you wire up the right UI at the right time: disable a submit button while `isPending` is true, show a success toast when `isSuccess` flips, or display an error banner when `isError` becomes true.

rows: The mutation function has started but not yet resolved
Show a spinner, disable the submit button
Show a success message or toast notification
Display an error message and retry option
The mutation has not been called yet, or has been reset
Enable the submit button and show the form
A function to return all mutation state to idle
Call after a successful submit to reuse the form

data.text: Here is the simplest usage pattern: import `useMutation`, define a `mutationFn`, and call `mutate()` from an event handler. Notice how we disable the button and show all three user-facing states.

data.content: A complete AddUserForm using useMutation with all three UI states rendered explicitly.

data.title: Accessible Form Patterns
data.text: Always associate inputs with labels using htmlFor/id, use role="alert" for error messages, and disable the button during mutation to prevent double-submission.

After a successful mutation, the form may still show `isSuccess = true` on the next render cycle. Call `mutation.reset()` after handling success to return the mutation to its idle state. This is essential when a form is reused â€” such as an edit form that stays mounted after saving.

data.title: Resetting Mutation State
data.content: Using reset() after a successful save so the same form can be used again.

data.title: Reset After Success, Not Before
data.text: Call mutation.reset() inside onSuccess after you have processed the result. Calling it before will discard the error state before the user can read it.

useMutation accepts several lifecycle callbacks. Each has a distinct purpose: `onMutate` runs before the request (ideal for optimising UI), `onSuccess` runs after a successful response, `onError` handles failures, and `onSettled` always runs last, regardless of outcome.

data.title: Mutation Callbacks
items: onMutate(variables) â€” fires before the mutationFn. Cancel in-flight queries here and snapshot previous cache state.
onSuccess(data, variables, context) â€” fires after the mutation succeeds. Great place to invalidate related queries.
onError(error, variables, context) â€” fires if the mutation fails. Use this to roll back optimistic updates.
onSettled(data, error, variables, context) â€” always fires last. Use it for cleanup that must run regardless of outcome.

data.title: Watch Out For
items: Calling mutate() inside the render body â€” it will fire on every render. Use an event handler instead.
Forgetting to invalidate related queries â€” the cache stays stale after a write.
Using the old onSuccess queryKey syntax â€” in v5, call invalidateQueries on the queryClient instance directly.
Not disabling the submit button â€” leads to duplicate requests and confusing UI.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Todo Creator
data.description: Create a form that uses useMutation to add a new todo to a list fetched by useQuery.
steps: Set up a useQuery for fetching todos from /api/todos.
Create an AddTodoForm component using useMutation to POST new todos.
Invalidate the ['todos'] query in onSuccess so the list refreshes automatically.
Show isPending to disable the submit button while saving.
Show isSuccess to display a brief confirmation message.
Show isError to display an error message with the actual error text.
Call mutation.reset() on success so the form can be reused.
Add input validation: prevent submitting empty todos.
data.expectedOutcome: A working form that adds a todo, refreshes the list via cache invalidation, disables the button during save, and shows clear success or error messages.

data.text: Mutations are not automatically executed â€” they sit idle until you call mutate. This design gives you full control over when side effects occur.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: useMutation is for create, update, and delete operations
Mutations are triggered manually via mutate() â€” they do not auto-run
isPending, isSuccess, and isError give you full UI control
Call mutation.reset() after success to make forms reusable
Always invalidate related queries in onSuccess to keep the cache fresh
data.takeaway: useMutation is the workhorse of data-changing operations. Master its state flags and lifecycle callbacks to build polished forms.
